source: The plain words behind every ? on a Safeword screen: what the box means, what counts, where to look, and what to do if unsure. Written for a person who has never filled in a form about this work before.
confidenceNote: Words, not numbers. Nothing here is written into a box.

stream.kind.what: What kind of earning this line is.
stream.kind.counts: One line per platform or per way of working. Two subscriber sites are two lines; sessions and doubles can be one.
stream.kind.where: The tab you open to see the money.
stream.kind.unsure: Pick the closest; the kind only sets the starting cuts and the risk word.

stream.label.what: A name for the line, for you.
stream.label.counts: A working name is enough: Sessions, the clip store, the app. Never a client, never a login.
stream.label.unsure: Leave it blank and the kind's name is used.

stream.typical.what: What a normal month brings in from this line, before anyone takes a cut.
stream.typical.counts: Gross: what clients and fans actually paid, before the platform's share, the processor's fee, and your own costs.
stream.typical.where: The platform's earnings tab for a few ordinary months; the booking notes; the cash count.
stream.typical.unsure: Take three months that were neither great nor dead and use the middle one.

stream.low.what: What a bad month brings in from this line, before cuts.
stream.low.counts: The kind of month that still happens: a slow season, a ban week, an illness. Not the worst month ever; the one that comes round each year.
stream.low.where: The lowest ordinary month in the last year.
stream.low.unsure: Half the typical month is a fair first guess for platform work; leave it blank rather than guess if you have no history.

stream.platformFee.what: The share the site keeps before paying you.
stream.platformFee.counts: Only the site's cut. A card fee on top of it goes in the next box.
stream.platformFee.where: The site's payout page or terms. It is a percent, usually 20 to 60.
stream.platformFee.unsure: Press “Use the common cuts” for a starting point, then check it against a real payout.

stream.processorFee.what: The share a card or transfer company keeps.
stream.processorFee.counts: Card fees on in-person or app payments, usually 2 to 4 percent. Zero if the site already took its cut and pays you direct.
stream.processorFee.where: The statement from the card reader or app.
stream.processorFee.unsure: 3 percent is the usual figure for cards; 0 for cash and for money already netted by a site.

stream.cashShare.what: The share of this line that arrives as cash.
stream.cashShare.counts: Cash in hand, no fee. Everything else is traceable and carries a fee.
stream.cashShare.where: Your own count; a few months of notes.
stream.cashShare.unsure: Sessions are often mostly cash; anything online is 0.

stream.monthsActive.what: How many months a year this line runs.
stream.monthsActive.counts: 12 if it runs all year. Fewer for touring seasons, a con circuit, a site you only work in winter.

stream.rail.what: Where this line's money lands first.
stream.rail.counts: The account, app, platform balance or cash box it arrives in before you move it.
stream.rail.where: The Rails page lists the places; add them there first.
stream.rail.unsure: Pick where most of it lands.

cost.kind.what: What kind of cost this is.
cost.kind.counts: The kind sets whether it is fixed and how a return usually treats it; both can be changed on the line.

cost.label.what: A name for the cost, for you.
cost.label.unsure: Leave it blank and the kind's name is used.

cost.month.what: What it costs in a normal month.
cost.month.counts: Yearly things divided by twelve: a con table, an annual listing, a shoot twice a year.
cost.month.where: Bank and card statements, the platform's invoice, receipts.
cost.month.unsure: Look at the last three months and take the middle.

cost.fixed.what: Whether the cost comes whether or not you work.
cost.fixed.counts: Fixed: rent, listings, the phone, the accountant. Varies: gear, travel, supplies that go up and down with sessions.
cost.fixed.unsure: If a dead month still gets the bill, it is fixed.

cost.deductible.what: How a tax pro who knows the work usually treats this kind on a return.
cost.deductible.counts: Usually: ordinary business costs. Sometimes: clothing, grooming and the look, which the rules only allow when unsuitable for daily life. Ask: health and anything personal that also serves the work.
cost.deductible.unsure: Leave the kind's word. The Taxes page counts only “usually” unless you tick the box there.

you.session.what: What one session or booking brings, before cuts.
you.session.counts: Your usual rate for a standard booking, not a special or a double.
you.session.unsure: Leave it blank; the page only needs it for the per-session figures.

you.sessionsMonth.what: How many sessions in a typical month.

you.filingStatus.counts: Single, head of household (you pay for a home with a dependent), married filing together, married filing apart.
you.filingStatus.where: The top of last year's return.

you.state.what: The state whose income tax applies to you.
you.state.counts: Where you live, in most cases. Nine states have no income tax and the list says so.
you.state.unsure: Leave it unchosen; the page shows a federal-only figure and says so.

taxes.countSometimes.what: Whether to count the “sometimes” costs, the look and the wardrobe, as deductions.
taxes.countSometimes.counts: Ticked: the jar assumes a tax pro will carry them. Unticked: the jar is sized as if they will not, which is the safer number.
taxes.countSometimes.unsure: Leave it unticked and ask a tax pro who knows the work.

taxes.setAsideRate.what: The share of the work's money you already move to a tax account when it lands.
taxes.setAsideRate.counts: Your current habit, not what the page suggests.
taxes.setAsideRate.unsure: If you have no habit yet, leave it blank; the page's figure is the one to start.

taxes.priorYearLiability.what: The total tax you owed last year, before what was paid in.
taxes.priorYearLiability.where: Last year's federal return, the line called total tax. Add the state's total tax if you file one.
taxes.priorYearLiability.unsure: Leave it blank; the page then plans on this year's estimate alone, without the safe harbour.

taxes.priorYearAgi.where: The line called adjusted gross income on last year's federal return.
taxes.priorYearAgi.unsure: Leave it blank. It only matters above $150,000, where the safe harbour asks for 110 percent.

taxes.paidThisYear.what: What you have paid toward this year's tax so far.
taxes.paidThisYear.counts: Estimated payments made this year. Not a job's withholding; the page counts that on its own.
taxes.paidThisYear.where: The payment confirmations, or the tax account.
taxes.paidThisYear.unsure: Zero if you have paid nothing; blank if you do not know.

personal.lean.what: What it costs you, personally, to stay housed and fed with every extra cut.
personal.lean.counts: Rent or your share of it, food, transport, medication, insurance, the phone, the minimum on any debt. Not the practice's costs; not the scene's.
personal.lean.where: Rent plus the last three months of groceries, transit and bills, averaged.
personal.lean.unsure: Rent doubled is a rough first figure for most cities.

personal.typical.what: What you actually spend on yourself in an ordinary month.
personal.typical.counts: The lean month plus what makes it a life: eating out, the gym, gifts, the cat. Not the practice's costs; the scene has its own page.
personal.typical.where: Three months of card and cash spending, averaged.
personal.typical.unsure: The lean month plus a third.

fund.targetMonths.what: How many months the fund should carry you with no money coming in.
fund.targetMonths.counts: Months of your lean month plus the house's fixed costs.
fund.targetMonths.unsure: Six. Three if a vanilla job covers the lean month on its own; nine if one platform is most of your income.

fund.setAsideRate.what: The share of each month's landed money that goes into the fund.
fund.setAsideRate.counts: A percent of what lands after cuts, moved the same day.
fund.setAsideRate.unsure: Ten percent until the fund is full; then it becomes the long game's.

rail.kind.what: What kind of place this is.
rail.kind.counts: A bank, a processor, a payment app, a platform balance not yet paid out, cash, crypto, prepaid cards.

rail.label.what: A name for the place, for you.
rail.label.counts: Bank A, the app, the cash box. Never the account number.
rail.label.unsure: Leave it blank and the kind's name is used.

rail.balance.what: What is in it right now.
rail.balance.counts: Today's balance. For a platform, the amount it shows as yours but has not sent.
rail.balance.unsure: Round it. A rough figure is better than a blank for the checks.

rail.closeRisk.what: How likely this place is to close or freeze on you because of the work.
rail.closeRisk.counts: High: adult work is against its terms, or it has closed people you know. Medium: it tolerates it but reviews. Low: it cannot be closed (cash, a wallet you hold) or has never blinked.

rail.forWork.what: Whether this place is the practice's or your own.
rail.forWork.counts: The practice's: work money lands here or its bills go out of here. My own: rent, groceries, the personal side.
rail.forWork.unsure: If both, say the practice's; the check only asks that at least one place is kept apart.

rail.isFund.what: Whether this place holds the safeword fund.
rail.isFund.counts: Tick every place whose balance is the fund. The Safeword page adds them up.
rail.isFund.unsure: The savings account nobody spends from.

you.age.unsure: It sets the years to the stop age and the over-50 catch-up.

longgame.account.what: The retirement account you put money in, or plan to.
longgame.account.counts: SEP IRA and Solo 401(k) are for the self-employed and take the most. Roth and traditional IRA are open to anyone with earned income. A job's 401(k) is the vanilla job's. A plain brokerage account has no limit and no shelter.
longgame.account.unsure: Roth IRA to start; SEP IRA once the profit is real. A tax pro can say which.

longgame.balance.what: What is in the account now.
longgame.balance.unsure: Zero if there is no account yet.

longgame.month.what: What you put in each month, on average.
longgame.month.counts: Yearly lump sums divided by twelve.
longgame.month.unsure: What you did last year, divided by twelve.

longgame.rate.what: How much you expect the money to grow a year, after inflation.
longgame.rate.counts: A percent. After inflation means the numbers stay in today's dollars.
longgame.rate.unsure: Five percent is the usual long-run guess for a mixed fund; four if you want to be careful.

longgame.stopAge.what: The age you want to stop needing to work.
longgame.stopAge.unsure: Sixty is a common answer; the page shows what the path reaches by then.

longgame.exitYear.what: The year you plan to step away from this work, or change how you do it.
longgame.exitYear.counts: A pivot, not a retirement: the year the sessions stop, or the content does, or you move to teaching only.
longgame.exitYear.unsure: Leave it blank if there is no such year in mind.

longgame.cushionMonths.what: How many lean months of cushion you want in hand the day you step away.
longgame.cushionMonths.counts: Months of your lean month, held in cash or the like, on top of the safeword fund.
longgame.cushionMonths.unsure: Twelve is the usual answer for a career change.

person.name.what: What to call this person here.
person.name.counts: A first name or a scene name. Nothing here leaves the browser.
person.name.unsure: Their role is fine as a name.

person.role.counts: Me is you; your numbers come from the other pages. The rest are words for the split and the protocol; they change no number.

person.income.what: What this person brings in a month, after tax.
person.income.unsure: Ask them, or leave it blank and choose equal shares.

person.lean.what: What this person needs a month to stay housed and fed.
person.lean.counts: Their own lean month, the way yours is on the Safeword page.
person.lean.unsure: Leave it blank; the floor check then says it cannot judge.

person.share.what: This person's agreed share of the shared month, as a percent.
person.share.counts: Only used when the split is “agreed shares”. All the shares must add to 100.
person.share.unsure: Switch the split to equal or in proportion.

house.shared.what: What the house costs a month, all in, for everyone.
house.shared.counts: Rent or mortgage, utilities, shared food, the internet, the pets. Not anyone's personal spending; not the practice's costs.
house.shared.where: The lease, the utility bills, the shared card.

house.splitRule.what: How the shared month is divided.
house.splitRule.counts: Equal: the same for everyone. In proportion: by income, so whoever earns more pays more in the same ratio. Agreed: shares you set.
house.splitRule.unsure: In proportion is the usual fair answer between people with different incomes.

protocol.from.counts: The giver: the one paying the allowance, the tribute, the drain.
protocol.from.unsure: Leave it as nobody if no money moves inside the dynamic.

protocol.to.unsure: Leave it as nobody if no money moves inside the dynamic.

protocol.amount.what: How much moves in a typical month.
protocol.amount.counts: The total across the month: a weekly tribute times four, an allowance, a drain.

protocol.cap.what: The most that can move in a month, agreed in advance.
protocol.cap.counts: A ceiling no scene raises. The check fails if the month's amount is above it, or if there is none.
protocol.cap.unsure: Set it at the usual amount until you have talked.

protocol.review.what: The day you both look at the numbers with the scene off.
protocol.review.counts: A date within the next year.

protocol.safeword.what: Whether there is a word that ends the money arrangement, no explanation owed, no penalty.
protocol.safeword.counts: Ticked only if you have both said so out loud.
protocol.safeword.unsure: Leave it unticked and have the talk.

play.kind.what: What kind of spending this line is.

play.label.what: A name for the line, for you.
play.label.unsure: Leave it blank and the kind's name is used.

play.year.what: What it costs in a year.
play.year.counts: The whole year: tickets, the hotel, the travel, the vendor hall; or the dues times twelve.
play.year.where: Last year's card statements around the events; the club's dues page.
play.year.unsure: Take last year and round up.

paper.will.what: The paper that says who gets what is not already spoken for, and who handles it.
paper.will.counts: Done: signed and witnessed the way your state requires, and someone knows where it is. Started: drafted, or an appointment booked.
paper.will.where: Many states have simple statutory forms; a lawyer who has seen a chosen family before is worth the fee.

paper.beneficiaries.what: The named person on every retirement account, life insurance policy and transfer-on-death form.
paper.beneficiaries.counts: Done: every account has a living, named person you chose. These forms outrank the will for what they cover.
paper.beneficiaries.where: The account's settings; the insurer's form.
paper.beneficiaries.unsure: Log in to each and look. Blank means the estate, which means the state's list.

paper.healthProxy.what: The paper that names who speaks for you in a hospital.
paper.healthProxy.counts: Done: signed, and the person has a copy. Some states call it a health care proxy or an advance directive.
paper.healthProxy.where: Most states have a free statutory form.

paper.financialPoa.what: The paper that lets someone pay your rent and reach your accounts if you cannot.
paper.financialPoa.counts: Done: signed and notarised if your state asks, and the bank has seen it.
paper.financialPoa.where: A statutory form in most states; the bank may have its own.

paper.digital.what: A file that says where the accounts, keys, codes and passwords are, and who may use them.
paper.digital.counts: Done: written down, kept somewhere safe, and one person knows how to open it. A platform balance dies with the login; a wallet dies with the keys.
paper.digital.unsure: Started, if a password manager exists and one person has the emergency access.

paper.names.what: A file that says which accounts, leases and bills are under which name.
paper.names.counts: Done: the working name and the legal name each have their list, and the person handling things can find both.
paper.names.unsure: Started, if you could write it in an evening.

paper.emergency.what: The plan for being hurt, held or arrested.
paper.emergency.counts: Done: one person knows who to call first, who has a key, who feeds the animals, and where the lawyer or bail money is.
paper.emergency.unsure: Started, if one person has the key.

paper.wishes.what: A letter, not a legal paper, that says what you want said and not said, and what happens to the content.
paper.wishes.counts: Done: written and kept with the will.
paper.wishes.unsure: Not yet. It is the last one, and the easiest.
